summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for shortness of breath, periumbilical abdominal pain, and worsening left leg pain. Her dyspnea was attributed to an acute on chronic diastolic heart failure exacerbation, with volume overload confirmed by elevated BNP, pulmonary edema on imaging, and response to diuresis. She was treated with increased furosemide and showed clinical improvement. Abdominal pain resolved during admission and was likely related to her heart failure, as CT showed no acute intra-abdominal pathology. A left leg infection was suspected due to a draining sinus tract and a positive blood culture for coagulase-negative staph, though repeat cultures were negative. Given her immunocompromised state and prior hardware, she was treated with vancomycin and discharged on minocycline pending orthopedic and infectious disease follow-up. Hypertension remained elevated but improved with pain control and medication adjustment. She was discharged home with services on optimized heart failure and infection management.
problems: Acute on chronic diastolic heart failure
Acute on chronic left lower extremity infection
